Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

capture verb

a town, a place

also take (a town), storm, seize, conquer (a city), capture of a city, retake a town, conquer a country, raze a town to the ground

classical

Sall. Jug. 92.3: pauca repugnantibus Numidīs capit (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 1.1.1: Trojā captā

capiō, capere, cēpī, captum

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

take, capture

The general word: a town, a camp, a ship is capta however it fell.

Other words

  • expugnō, expugnāre, expugnāvī, expugnātum — take by storm

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 2.12.2 (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    To take by assault, as opposed to oppugnāre, to attack (see attack): Caesar attacked Noviodunum on the march expugnāre nōn potuit, but could not take it.

  • potior, potīrī, potītus sum — gain possession of, become master of

    verb, fourth conjugation, deponent, with the ablative · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 2.7 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 295 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    With the ablative (oppidō potīrī); of anything one gets hold of, not only places.

Examples

  • id ex itinere oppugnāre cōnātus, expugnāre nōn potuit

    he tried to attack it on the march, but could not take itCaes. B.G. 2.12.2

  • oppidum recipere

    to retake a townTraupman 187; cf. Cic. de Or. 2.273 (Lewis & Short s.v. recipiō)

  • terrā potīrī

    to conquer a countryTraupman 186

  • oppidum solō aequāre

    to raze a town to the groundTraupman 187; cf. Vell. 2.4.2 (Lewis & Short s.v. solum)

See also capture, occupy, attack, defeat, war, prisoner.
